primitives.note: Clean Cuts: 0-5 stacks generated by ability casts (3 per cast); each basic attack consumes one stack to fire the empowered attack instead of a normal one.
Stacks cap at 5, each stack instance lasts 8s and refreshes on subsequent ability casts (not a damage buff per se, but a capped/expiring resource gated identically to the primitive).

P: empowered attack deals extra physical damage to other enemies hit (splash) beyond the primary target's normal attack damage. W: while buffed, every basic attack fires an extra feather dealing 25% of the triggering attack's damage on-hit.
Deadly Plumage grants 35-55% bonus attack speed for 4s on cast; also grants a movement-speed buff on champion hit (movement-only, ignored for damage fight).
Double Daggers fires two separately-timed missiles per cast; the second hit on a given target is reduced 50% relative to the first.
Q's cast time (and the attack lockout during it) shrinks with bonus attack speed down to a 0.1s floor, changing effective cast/attack tempo.
E deals damage instantly on cast (recalling planted feathers); R deals its damage on a fixed 1s delay after the leap.

Each successive feather beyond the first that hits the same target in one Bladecaller cast deals diminishing damage per an undisclosed formula (5% falloff per prior hit, capped at 10% of base beyond the 19th).

E's per-feather damage and P's empowered-attack secondary damage both scale up with the champion's crit chance/crit damage, even though the hit that lands cannot itself crit (E) or is reduced-crit (P).
Featherstorm blocks basic attacks and other ability casts for its ~1.5s duration (Xayah can still move) before dealing damage.
Mana costs (35/40-60/20/100, plus regen) may constrain how many casts of each ability fit in a 15s fight depending on mana pool/regen from build.

The number of feathers that actually pass through and hit the lone dummy when Bladecaller is cast depends on how many feathers were planted by prior Q casts/empowered attacks and their ground geometry relative to the target — this count directly feeds the diminishing-returns damage formula.
The ghosted/untargetable window (1.25-1.5s, sources disagree) only matters for damage taken/survival, not for the damage fight.

needsBespoke.why: Bladecaller's damage is not a flat per-hit or per-stack value: it is 'damage of one feather' multiplied by a disclosed-but-nonstandard diminishing-returns formula over n, where n is the count of feathers that hit the target in that cast. That count is itself a simulation-dependent quantity driven by how many feathers Xayah has planted via Q casts and empowered autoattacks (Clean Cuts) before E is cast, and by geometry (how many of those planted feathers' return paths pass through the single dummy). No primitive in the closed list captures 'a formula over a self-generated, history-dependent hit count'; conditional-damage and positional-assumption together only flag the pieces, they do not encode the n-dependent falloff formula itself.

unsettled.question: When Double Daggers is cast at a single stationary dummy, do both daggers actually strike that one target (first at full damage, second at 50% reduced, per 'targets hit after the first take 50% reduced damage'), or are the two daggers fired on separate left/right offset lines such that only one connects with a lone target standing on Xayah's centerline?
options: Both daggers hit the single target every cast: total damage = 1x base + 0.5x base (the wiki's 'Total Reduced Damage' row, i.e. 1.5x per-hit base plus AD ratio)
Only one dagger reliably hits a single centered target (the width/offset geometry means the second dagger travels down an offset line and misses a single dummy): total damage = 1x base only
Depends on assumed target/caster positioning, which the dummy fight must define

proposal: Enter the fight already auto-attacking to have Clean Cuts stacks and planted Feathers available immediately.
Cast Q (Double Daggers) as the opener to plant Feathers on the ground and generate 3 Clean Cuts stacks.
Weave in empowered basic attacks (consuming Clean Cuts stacks) between ability casts whenever a stack is available.
Cast W (Deadly Plumage) early to gain the attack-speed buff, which also speeds up Q's cast time and increases autoattack frequency for the rest of the fight.
Once several Feathers are planted (from the opening Q and empowered autoattacks), cast E (Bladecaller) to recall them for a burst hit and stack generation.
Cast R (Featherstorm) for its flat AD-scaled burst damage, accepting its ~1.5s window where Xayah cannot attack or cast (only reasonable once, given a 100-140s cooldown far exceeding the 15s fight).
Continue autoattacking (empowered by Clean Cuts and W's extra feather) throughout, refreshing Q and E off cooldown as they come up, and recasting E again whenever enough new Feathers have landed.
Track mana spend against the champion's mana pool/regen; if mana runs out, prioritize autoattacks (which don't cost mana) over marginal ability casts.
questions: Should R be cast immediately for guaranteed burst, or held/skipped in a 15s single-target dummy fight since its animation costs ~1.5s of lost autoattack/Q/E uptime?
Given the unsettled feather-count question, how many times can E realistically be cast in 15s, and does it matter whether Q is cast before or after each E to maximize planted feathers for the recall?
Does the sim assume max ranks (5/5/5/3) and full runes/items from level 1, or a leveling curve, since ability ranks change Q/E/W numbers and R rank-1 availability?
Should autoattacks be paused to avoid the Q cast-time attack lockout, or does the simulator handle attack-timer/cast-time interaction automatically?
